conviction_note: Two weak findings that net to +1.0. A modest Q2 EPS beat against a $0.63 bar that sits about 36% under the $0.98 comp, on a name whose last print with the guide held paid +15%, offset by a small negative: the H2-weighted guide depends on an end-market recovery the August ABI does not show. Both are inference from public data rather than a primary-document fact, so the size stays at about a tenth of the 12.7% median reaction.
bar: Adjusted EPS $0.63 for Q2 FY27. Sources: MarketBeat/Defense World preview (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-apogee-enterprises-apog-set-to-release-quarterly-earnings-on-tuesday-2026-09-29/) and a second consensus snippet ($0.63 on $346.7M). The two revenue figures disagree ($359.5M vs $346.7M, probably over whether Kalwall is in), so revenue is not used as the bar. Company guide, directional only: Q2 'net sales slightly lower and adjusted EPS lower year over year' against $358.2M and $0.98 (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/06/26/apogee-apog-q1-2027-earnings-call-transcript/). FY27 guide $2.70-$3.25 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/6845/000000684526000058/a53026fy27q1results.htm).
positioning_check: Short interest 4.57% of float, 4.24 days to cover, up 11.3% (MarketBeat, via search snippet, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/APOG/, about mid-September 2026 settlement). Not crowded. No usable option chain (open interest 0), so there is no skew and no implied move. The baseline falls back to the median historical reaction, 12.72%. Tape: -5.9% over 20 days, -27.7% from the 52-week high, about -18% since the Aug 5 grant price of $42.96.

findings.finding: The Q2 bar of $0.63 adjusted EPS is 36% below the $0.98 comp and below the run-rate that Q1 implies. The company guided only 'lower YoY' and is H2-weighted. In Q1 the street sat at $0.43, 23% under the comp, and the company printed $0.57, flat YoY. The same conservatism looks embedded again, so the base case is a print of about $0.66-0.70.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 (2026-06-26): a $0.14 EPS beat with the guide maintained gave +15.16%. Q2 FY26 (Oct 2025): an EPS beat with the FY guide lowered gave -4.44%. Jan 2026 and Jan 2025, where guidance was cut: -13.89% and -19.02%. Beats are paid only when the guide holds.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market expected another beat on thin coverage, the stock would not have given back all of the +15% Q1 reaction and fallen about 18% since August with no company-specific negative filing. The Aug 31 Zacks downgrade to hold suggests estimates stopped rising rather than that a beat is being underwritten. This is weak evidence: an unexplained drawdown is not itself a finding.
findings.independence: Q2 FY26 comp of $0.98 from the company's own 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/6845/000000684525000154/a83025fy26q2results.htm). The same company guide caveat applies: 'lower YoY' covers anything from $0.63 to $0.97. Partly caveated: the $0.98 comp included a $4.6M NMTC gain, so the underlying comp is lower and the gap is smaller than it looks.

findings.finding: The FY27 guide assumes H2 'improvement in underlying market conditions', but the AIA/Deltek ABI was 47.2 in August 2026 ('continue to decline', the longest slump in the index's history; institutional 47.0). That puts the H2-weighted guide at risk on the Q2 call, where the low end ($2.70) or the H2 shape could be questioned.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance is the line this stock trades on: -19.02% (Jan 2025) and -13.89% (Jan 2026) on cuts, -4.44% (Oct 2025) on a lowered FY guide despite a beat, +15.16% (Jun 2026) on a maintained guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the ABI is public and the stock is down about 18% since August. What would be visible if it were fully priced: the low end of the guide treated as the bar. The consensus EPS still implies about $1.78 in H2, near the guide midpoint. This is macro-to-company transmission. The company has only said glass softness reflects 'fewer jobs', so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Q1 call: management said results would be 'weighed more heavily towards the second half of the year reflecting anticipated improvement in underlying market conditions', and Glass is under 'softer conditions in new construction' (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/06/26/apogee-apog-q1-2027-earnings-call-transcript/). AIA's own release says the same as the ABI source (https://www.aia.org/resource-center/abi-august-2026-architecture-firm-billings-continue-decline). Counterweights: the Services backlog of $734.5M is up 8% YoY, and Tecnoglass's Aug 6 print showed record commercial backlog (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/06/3340090/0/en/tecnoglass-reports-second-quarter-2026-results-including-record-revenues-on-continued-market-share-gains.html). That is why this is small.

outside_window.finding: PMC Property Group's defective-glass suit (nickel sulfide, three Philadelphia towers) survived a motion to dismiss on the manufacturing-defect claim against Wausau and Viracon. Apogee itself was dismissed for lack of personal jurisdiction. There is no dated catalyst in the window.

searched_and_found_nothing: IEEPA tariff refund: neither the Q1 FY27 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000006845/000000684526000063/apog-20260530.htm) nor the Q1 call mentions IEEPA or refunds. Apogee's tariff exposure is Section 232 aluminum, which is not refundable.

EDGAR 8-Ks since June (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0000006845.json): director elections (Aug 5, Sep 14), the GroGlass agreement (Sep 2) and its completion (Sep 23), the S-8 (Aug 20). No negative 8-K, no departures, no 2.02 pre-announcement.

GroGlass ($72.5M, about $30M revenue at about 25% EBITDA margin, funded by cash and the revolver; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/6845/000000684526000087/ex991-apogacquisitionann.htm): it closed after the quarter end, details are promised for the Q2 call, and the EPS effect is roughly neutral after interest. Financing buys an acquisition and is not distress, so no sign.
Kalwall closed July 1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000006845/000000684526000068/ex991.htm). It is already in the pro forma guide and is EPS-neutral per management.
Insider Form 4s since June: only grants, RSUs and director awards. No open-market cluster.

Aluminum: the Midwest premium sat near record through Jun-Aug, then fell 8-12% on Aug 21 on a Canadian tariff-cut signal (https://aegis-hedging.com/insights/metals/daily-first-look/2026-08-21). Surcharges pass it through with a lag and Q1 Metals margins expanded despite it, so the sign is unclear and it was not filed.
WARN and layoff notices: only the Nov 2025 Mesquite TX closure (58 jobs), already known. Nothing for 2026.
The Sep 1 -5.4% drop: no catalyst found in the coverage (https://www.dailypolitical.com/2026/09/01/apogee-enterprises-nasdaqapog-shares-down-5-4-heres-what-happened.html).
baseline_tension: There is no skew or implied move to agree or disagree with. The small positive cuts against the falling tape (-5.9% over 20 days, -18% since August), which may reflect the same end-market worry that finding 2 carries. That worry is why the net is only +1.0 against a 12.7% median reaction.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis until the company says it): the ABI/H2-guide finding was cut from -1.0 to -0.5. It was not dropped, because management did tie its H2 guide to market improvement and the Glass softness to 'fewer jobs'.
Rule 7 (look up short interest before a negative): 4.57% of float and 4.24 days to cover is not crowded, so the negative was not shrunk further.

Rule 6 (verify the bar): the EPS bar of $0.63 agrees across two sources but the revenue bar disagrees ($359.5M vs $346.7M), so revenue was not used. The finding lands inside the company's directional guide, which caps it as a reported-quarter item: left at +1.5, not raised.

Rules 1 and 8 (reaction function, thin coverage): this name pays on the guide. Left finding 1 at +1.5 rather than raising it toward the 12.7% median, because it is inference from the bar's conservatism and not a confirmed, document-level unpriced number.
Rule 6 (exit window): the PMC litigation was moved to outside_window.
